item.title: Good mysteries come in small packages.
item.content:encoded:
Perfectly applicable to this proposal, as well as the functionality of SCP-001 itself. The article does not give too much, nor too little, and respects the reader's imagination to theorize what wonders/horrors are contained within (and thereby kept out.) Basically another one of those instances where the SCP in question isn't the subject you should be fearing.

Since there is a keyhole, is it meant to be unlocked? If so, by whom? If it is meant to be locked away for all eternity, who (or what) is the reason for its imprisonment? These questions will never be answered, but they're fun to ask anyway.

item.title: not_a_seagull's SCP Oddessy: qntm's Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Item #: SCP-001 (qntm's Proposal)

Author: qntm

Review:

+ Review
- Review

A criticism of this SCP is that it's not really that big, like an 001 is supposed to be. However, this was before 001 was considered to be "big," so I'll give it a pass on that.

In all honesty, I love this proposal. Unlike the newer 001's, which great overarching story and narrative1, this skip is short, sweet, and leaves behind ground-shattering implications.

In my headcanon2, we're Apakht. The universe is what's trapped inside this gemstone, and somebody doesn't want it to get out. Either somebody realized the implications of this and locked the gem up so our universe doesn't flow into our universe, creating a paradox, or something more sinister, it's locked up tight.

In addition, the Project Charon storyline will probably expand this story by at least 17 miles. So I'm looking forwards to that.

Verdict: Upvote

Footnotes
1. Which isn't a bad thing, I assure you.
2. You can have your own, obviously.

item.content:encoded: I like this article, but one thing about it bothers me: there's no such thing as Sumerian runes. The writing system used for Sumerian is called cuneiform. "Runes" specifically refers to the Germanic Futhark and its variants as well as certain visually similar alphabetic writing systems such as the Old Hungarian alphabet. It's not a big thing but as a linguistics hobbyist, it takes me out of the article in the same way that a historical or physical science inaccuracy would for many readers.

item.title: Re: Great, but not 1
item.content:encoded:
The other 001 proposals assume that they're just indexed in order (which makes perfect sense) or theyre classified in order of importance (which makes some slight sense, in theory, but isn't born out).

Wait, really? Maybe it just slipped my mind, but I don't remember any 001 proposals indicating this.

If it's not one of those, what is it?

I personally assumed that numerical designations were sort of picked from open slots, sort of like the way the site currently works (albeit maybe without designation replacement, because in-universe what is a downvote??). After all, indexing by order of discovery seems silly when the Foundation is a worldwide presence and there's always the possibility SCPs might be recovered together or at the same time. Indexing by order of importance also wouldn't make sense because then the item numbers would be constantly changing as new SCPs are discovered.

And if SCP designations are irrelevant, if which SCP is designated 001 is irrelevant, why is there a separate page for 001 proposals with a mnemetic kill agent and decoys and stuff.

SCP designations other than 001, in-universe, I would think would be largely irrelevant. 001 is special. (also 000. Shh.)

Obviously, SCP-001 is supposed to be different somehow, and for me, this doesn't have that ring to it.

Maybe read through the author's comments in this discussion page? Admittedly, it's not the easiest thing to grasp after the first reading, but this is definitely different from a mainlist entry.

item.content:encoded: I love this, and I downvoted it. Not because there is anything I don't love about this SCP but because I can't for the life of me think of an excuse for it to be designated SCP-001. The writing makes it seem obvious to me that it was discovered WELL into the Foundation's history, and if the numbers don't designate order of classificaton, I don't know what they mean. If you try to say it's part of a collection of the first batch of SCPs, you're saying the Living Room and the Biological Motherboard were in the Cabinet of Curiosities, which is kind of weird to picture, and probably the Twelve Rusty Keys AND THE DOOR, which I flatly refuse to consider. If it were any other number, I would upvote without a second thought.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
After standing back and reflecting on this thing for a little while I've finally worked out what's wrong with it. This SCP is a collision between two mutually exclusive ideas:

(1) The artifact contains our entire universe and in fact is our whole universe in microcosm. Damaging it could damage the whole universe.
(2) Our universe in its entirety is either an SCP or the container for some gargantuan cosmic SCP which is itself being held under Secure Containment by some massive higher-dimensional Foundation.

Obviously it's kind of confusing for *both* of these things to be true simultaneously. It would be better to select one or the other. Option (1) has merit, but is a little too Futuramary and simplistic. I think option (2) has much more dramatic possibility, since it would imply that there is a universe-sized malevolent SCP trapped inside our universe and *we are trapped inside with it*. All the Foundation's other acquisitions could be manifestations of this same terrible thing. Or perhaps, humanity as a whole could be this SCP.
